documents.title: Emergency Department Admission Note
documents.content_text: 55yo male with hypertension and T2D presents with 2 hours of crushing substernal chest pressure radiating to left jaw, diaphoresis, and mild dyspnea. Initial BP 162/98 mmHg, HR 96 bpm. ECG reveals 2mm ST-elevation in leads V2-V4. Urgent cath lab activation initiated.

diagnostic_reports.conclusion: Troponin I critically elevated at 1.82 ng/mL (reference < 0.04 ng/mL). Consistent with acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction.

documents.title: Pulmonology Inpatient Discharge Summary
documents.content_text: 29yo female admitted for status asthmaticus refractory to home albuterol. Received IV methylprednisolone pulse, continuous nebulized bronchodilators, and supplemental oxygen. SpO2 normalized to 98% on ambient air. Discharged on fluticasone/salmeterol DPI.

diagnostic_reports.conclusion: Bilateral pulmonary hyperinflation with flattened diaphragms. No focal consolidation, pneumothorax, or acute pleural effusion.

documents.title: Cardiology Outpatient Follow-up
documents.content_text: 71yo male with ischemic cardiomyopathy (LVEF 30%) and NYHA Class III heart failure. Reports increasing peripheral edema (+2 pitting) and two-pillow orthopnea over 1 week. Medication adherence to carvedilol and sacubitril/valsartan verified. Upped furosemide to 80mg daily.

diagnostic_reports.conclusion: NT-proBNP markedly elevated at 4,820 pg/mL (normal < 450 pg/mL), indicating acute decompensated congestive heart failure.

documents.title: Neurology Outpatient Evaluation
documents.content_text: 38yo female presents with 3-week history of throbbing unilateral temporal headaches with scintillating scotoma and nausea. Symptoms worsen with physical exertion. Cranial nerve exam intact without focal sensorimotor deficit.

diagnostic_reports.code_display: MRI Brain with & without Gadolinium Contrast
diagnostic_reports.conclusion: No acute intracranial hemorrhage or mass effect. Mild punctate white matter hyperintensities in frontoparietal regions, likely microvascular/migrainous in etiology.
